Complete its perimeter: fill every blank cell across the top and bottom rows between the min/max occupied columns, and every blank cell down the left and right columns between the min/max occupied rows. Also complete full-height vertical rails inside the box at any interior column that contains foreground marks in interior rows (not just marks limited to the top/bottom border). Fill that rail from bounding-box top to bottom with 2, preserving existing foreground cells. Do not connect interior horizontal alignments. Demos confirmed this with varying backgrounds/foregrounds: an inner vertical rail at c7/c8 had dots near both ends and its missing cells were filled; on the solved 21x15 instance (background 1, foreground 9), bbox rows 1..20 and cols 3..12 (0-based), the outer perimeter plus full-height inner rail c10 were required. A previous partial interpolation of c10 only between its first/last 9s was wrong; the rail extended to both edges. The only other changes are on these frame/rail cells; preserve all original dots and leave remaining background unchanged.', path='arc', global_=True); print(updated.id, updated.version)
